cardiac_arrest.name: Cardiac Arrest — CPR & AED

steps.detail: Tap shoulders and shout 'Are you OK?'
If alone, put phone on speaker
Look for chest rise for 10 seconds
Heel of hand on center of chest, push hard and fast, 100-120/min, full recoil
30:2 ratio if trained, compression-only if untrained
Turn on AED, follow voice prompts, ensure no one touching patient
Switch compressors every 2 minutes to prevent fatigue

key_points: Push hard (at least 5 cm) and fast (100-120/min)
Allow full chest recoil between compressions
Minimize interruptions in compressions
Compression-only CPR is effective for untrained bystanders
AED use dramatically improves survival — use it as soon as available

choking_adult.name: Choking — Conscious Adult

steps.detail: Can they cough, speak, breathe? If yes, encourage coughing
Stand behind person, wrap arms around waist
Make fist above navel, thrust inward and upward

steps.action: Repeat until object expelled or person becomes unconscious
steps.detail: Each thrust should be a separate attempt

steps.action: If unconscious: lower to ground, begin CPR
steps.detail: Look in mouth before each breath, remove visible object

key_points: Ask 'Are you choking? Can you speak?' first
For pregnant or obese persons: chest thrusts instead of abdominal
Self-administered: make a fist above navel, thrust inward and upward
Infants (<1 year): 5 back slaps + 5 chest thrusts

severe_bleeding.name: Severe Bleeding Control

steps.detail: Put on gloves if available
Use clean cloth, press firmly on wound
Add more layers on top

steps.action: If bleeding doesn't stop, apply tourniquet
steps.detail: Place 5-8 cm above wound, tighten until bleeding stops, note time

steps.action: Elevate the injured limb above heart level
steps.detail: While maintaining pressure

steps.action: Keep person warm, treat for shock
steps.detail: Cover with blanket, elevate legs if no spinal injury

key_points: Apply firm, continuous pressure for at least 10 minutes
Tourniquets save lives — don't be afraid to use one
Note the time of tourniquet application
Remove clothing from around the wound

stroke.name: Stroke Recognition & Response (FAST)

steps.detail: Ask person to smile. Is one side drooping?
Ask person to raise both arms. Does one drift down?
Ask person to repeat a simple sentence. Is speech slurred?
Note exact time symptoms began — critical for treatment
Keep person calm, lying on affected side if vomiting, do NOT give food/drink

key_points: Time is brain — every minute counts
Do NOT drive to hospital yourself — call 112
Note the exact time symptoms started
Do NOT give aspirin (could be hemorrhagic stroke)
Keep airway clear if vomiting

burns.name: Burns — First Aid

steps.detail: Stop the burning process
Run cool (not ice cold) water for 10-20 minutes
From burned area, unless stuck to skin
Do NOT use butter, toothpaste, or home remedies
Ibuprofen or acetaminophen

key_points: Cool with running water for 10-20 minutes
NEVER use ice, butter, toothpaste, or oil on burns
For chemical burns: flush with large amounts of water for 20+ minutes
For electrical burns: do NOT touch person if still in contact with source
Seek emergency care for burns larger than palm, on face/hands/joints, or circumferential

severity_levels.treatment: Cool water, aloe vera, OTC pain relief
Cool water, sterile dressing, seek medical care

allergic_reaction.name: Anaphylaxis — Severe Allergic Reaction

steps.detail: Hives, swelling (face/throat), difficulty breathing, rapid pulse, dizziness
Outer thigh (through clothing if needed), hold 10 seconds
Even after EpiPen, anaphylaxis can recur
Unless breathing is difficult — then allow them to sit up
After 5-15 minutes if symptoms persist
If person stops breathing

key_points: EpiPen first, 112 second (but do both)
EpiPen goes in outer thigh — can inject through clothing
Always call 112 even after EpiPen — biphasic reaction possible
Common triggers: peanuts, tree nuts, shellfish, bee stings, medications, latex

fainting.name: Fainting (Syncope)

steps.detail: If they appear about to faint
About 30 cm above heart level
Look for head injury from fall
Collar, belt, tie

steps.action: Do NOT put anything in mouth
steps.detail: Myth: they won't swallow tongue

key_points: Most fainting is harmless but can indicate serious conditions
Seek medical care if: first faint, chest pain, prolonged unconsciousness, injury
Warning signs: lightheadedness, nausea, tunnel vision, sweating

types.name: Heat Stroke (EMERGENCY)
treatment: Cool rapidly with any means (ice, cold water)
Do NOT give fluids if unconscious

steps.detail: Remove wet clothing
Neck, head, chest, groin — use skin-to-skin contact if needed
Only if conscious and able to swallow
Rough movement can cause cardiac arrest
Confusion, slurred speech, drowsiness, loss of consciousness

steps.action: Do NOT move the injured area
steps.detail: Splint in position found
Splint above and below the injury
20 minutes on, 20 minutes off
If possible without moving fracture
Feel for pulse, check color/warmth below injury

snakebite.name: Snakebite

steps.action: Call 108 and get to a hospital with antivenom
steps.detail: Government hospitals stock anti-snake venom; go even if the bite looks small

steps.action: Keep the person still and calm
steps.detail: Movement spreads venom faster; carry them if you can

steps.action: Keep the bitten limb still, like a fracture
steps.detail: Loose splint, at heart level

steps.action: Remove rings, bangles, anklets and tight clothing
steps.detail: The limb may swell

steps.action: Do NOT cut, suck, tie a tight tourniquet, apply ice or herbs
steps.detail: These cause harm and delay treatment

key_points: Note the time of the bite; do not try to catch or kill the snake
Krait bites can be painless and happen at night; drowsiness or drooping eyelids need hospital care at once

poisoning.name: Poisoning (including pesticides)

steps.action: Call 108, or the AIIMS poison information centre 1800-116-117
steps.detail: Say what was swallowed, how much and when

steps.action: Do NOT make the person vomit
steps.detail: Unless a doctor or the poison centre tells you to

steps.action: Remove contaminated clothes and wash skin with water
steps.detail: For pesticides on skin; protect your own hands

steps.action: Lay them on their side if drowsy
steps.detail: Recovery position keeps the airway clear

steps.action: Take the container or strip to hospital
steps.detail: It tells doctors what to treat

key_points: If someone swallowed poison on purpose, stay with them; Tele-MANAS 14416 can help afterwards

medical.reply:
What you describe can be an emergency, and it needs a person, not an app.

Right now:
1. Call 112 (or 108 for an ambulance).
2. Stop any activity. Sit or lie down somewhere safe.
3. Do not drive yourself. Unlock the door and tell someone nearby.
4. Note when it started. Responders will ask.

Open the Emergency tab to share your medical ID with responders.

self_harm.reply:
I'm really glad you told me. You don't have to handle this alone.

Right now:
1. Call Tele-MANAS on 14416 (free, 24/7, in your language), or iCall on 9152987821.
2. If you might act on these thoughts, call 112 or go to the nearest hospital.
3. Move away from anything you could hurt yourself with, and stay near someone you trust.
4. Tell one person how you feel today, even in a single message.

I'm still here if you want to keep talking.
